tier_reason: The only baseline comparison (RIOT forum: 45/87 us against 74/131 us for RIOT's default C AES on an STM32L151) could not be opened (forum.riot-os.org, eprint.iacr.org and sacworkshop.org all fail with getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), so it rests on search snippets; the repo README gives absolute cycle counts with public Makefile flags but no baseline, and the SAC 2016 paper's 'about twice as fast as existing implementations' was seen in an abstract snippet only, without its comparison table.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: README cycle counts: arm-none-eabi-gcc (version unstated) with libopencm3, -O3 -mthumb -mcpu=cortex-m3 -msoft-float for the STM32L100C (M3) builds and -O3 -mthumb -mcpu=cortex-m4 -mfloat-abi=hard -mfpu=fpv4-sp-d16 for the STM32F407 (M4) builds, per aes128ctr/Makefile; the RIOT forum timings state no compiler or flags in the snippet.
corrections.caveats: The repo README has absolute cycle numbers but compares against nothing, and does not mention reference C AES or mbedTLS. The two comparison datapoints (RIOT forum timings, 'about twice as fast' in the SAC 2016 paper 'All the AES You Need on Cortex-M3 and M4') come from search-result snippets only: eprint.iacr.org, ko.stoffelen.nl, sacworkshop.org (slides) and forum.riot-os.org all fail to resolve here (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), so tier is capped at C and the paper's comparison table was not read; a verifier with paper access should check whether it supports B (the slides list it as the fastest T-table AES-CTR and bytesliced AES-128-CTR on these cores). The forum post gives no compiler flags or clock speed in the snippet. Makefiles are public (-O3, arm-none-eabi-gcc, version unstated). Repo is old (last commit 2020-07-12, 'Fix push wrong changes to aes128ctr'); CC0 dedication has no patent grant. Later Cortex-M AES work exists (jnk0le/cortexm-AES, whose CM3_1T code is based on this repo, and aadomn/aes fixslicing) and was not compared here. The T-table implementations are not constant-time (only the bitsliced variants are).

notes: Real SAC 2016 artifact (CC0, 97 stars, last commit 2020-07-12, abandoned) with public Makefile flags and README cycle counts, but every baseline comparison sits behind hosts unreachable from this container; kept at C. A paper-access retier could lift it to B if the SAC 2016 table names the prior implementations it beats.

tier_reason: Commit 3caa605 (Stephan Mueller, 2024-11-24) states 'The performance almost doubles: ml-kem/tests/kyber_kem_tester_common c - C: 123s - ASM: 65s' (1.89x, derived from page data); the test code is public but no board, compiler, flags or parameter set are given, so it is a first-party single-run figure at tier C.

corrections.workload: Wall-clock time of ml-kem/tests/kyber_kem_tester_common run with the 'c' argument, which in the current tester source (any argument other than e, d or k) runs 50,000 rounds of keygen, encapsulation and decapsulation; parameter set not stated in the commit message (the maintainer's later PQRV issue comment uses ML-KEM-1024 with the same 50,000 rounds). C build against the RISC-V RV64IM assembly build.
corrections.caveats: Lead in the task named 'Issue #2' of leancrypto; that issue is an unrelated Linux-kernel Kbuild error (opened 2023-06-27). The ~60% figure is in issue #2 of Ji-Peng/PQRV, 'Spacemit X60: RVV implementation causes SIGBUS' (opened 2024-11-24, closed 2024-11-26): a maintainer comment dated 2025-02-02 says 'Performance boost by almost 60% on Spacemit X60: for ML-KEM 1024 when performing 50,000 rounds of keygen/enc/dec, with RISCV asm it takes about 49.3s vs 31s with RVV 256' (derived 1.59x). That compares RVV-256 against the RISC-V assembly path, not against C, and was run on a SpacemiT X60 (VLEN=256) with no compiler or flags stated. The commit-message figure names no board, compiler, flags or parameter set and the test harness may have changed since; it is a first-party single-run anecdote. The RISC-V kernels are derived from Ji-Peng/PQRV (MIT; ml-kem/src/riscv64/ntt_dualissue_plant_rv64im.S says 'This file is derived from https://github.com/Ji-Peng/PQRV'), which is already verified in wave 13 at tier A, so this entry is largely a second claim on PQRV's kernels inside a different library. No bench tables exist in the repo README (only a performance goal statement). Licence is inferred from LICENSE.bsd and LICENSE.gplv2 (dual BSD-3-Clause/GPL-2.0 is assumed, the LICENSE file says 'See LICENSE.* for the applicable license'); the repo also carries per-file MIT, Apache-2.0, CC0 and GPL-3 (duplicated compiler code) notices from upstream sources, all OSI or public domain.

notes: Numbers match the commit message exactly (C 123 s, ASM 65 s; commit dated 2024-11-24); tier C stands. The ML-KEM RISC-V and RVV kernels are derived from Ji-Peng/PQRV (already verified A in wave 13); the orchestrator may treat this as a second claim on PQRV (duplicate with a paper: id) or keep it as the library that ships those kernels.
